chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The intellect is the guide of the believer.

key_terms.الدليل: Dalil — guide, proof, evidence; that which leads one to the truth
key_terms.العقل: 'Aql — intellect, reason; a divine faculty in Shia theology that guides toward truth
key_terms.المؤمن: Al-Mu'min — the believer, one with true faith (iman)

ai.seo_question: What is the role of intellect ('aql) in Islamic faith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirmed that the intellect ('aql) serves as the guide and distinguishing mark of a true believer. In Shia theological thought, 'aql is considered a divine faculty by which a person can distinguish truth from falsehood and navigate the path to God. This teaching is central to the Book of Intellect and Ignorance (Kitab al-'Aql wa'l-Jahl) in al-Kafi, where the Imam repeatedly elevates reason as the foundation of religious life.
